title: Phones and gear
purpose: We know every phone, mount, and charger. We know where each one is and who has it. This includes the ones at a partner's location.
how: Every phone is enrolled in Apple Business Manager and managed through Hexnode in supervised mode. That gives us a live map, lost mode, wipe from anywhere, and an inventory record that matches what we really have. The collection app is locked in kiosk mode. App updates go out in stages, so a client update never surprises the whole fleet.

Partner fleets are enrolled too. Phones with delivery partners belong to the company and only sit at someone else's location. If a partnership goes bad, the MDM is the only control we still have over them.

One registry is the only record we trust. Each phone has a row with the asset tag, serial number, IMEI, model, storage size, condition, current site, and current holder. It also logs every custody event: issued, returned, transferred, repaired, or lost.
The Planning and Logistics Lead owns the registry, the store, and the weekly count. The store is the Central Cairo warehouse.

breaks.do: Find the phone on the MDM map and put it in lost mode within one hour. You have 24 hours to get it back. After that, wipe it, file a police report, and update the registry. Any deduction follows the handbook, and only after Moharam reviews the case.

breaks.what: A site does not have enough hats or chargers
breaks.do: Use the kit spares first, then the store. A shortage is the Planning and Logistics Lead's failure, not the site's, and is fixed the same day.

breaks.what: An update to the collection app breaks something
breaks.do: Every update goes to two test phones first, always. The rest of the fleet gets it only after a full test shift passes on those two.

breaks.what: Something is stolen at a site
breaks.do: The site agreement makes the site responsible for theft at its location. Our property insurance covers the rest. Update the registry and tell the insurance company the same day.

breaks.what: A partner refuses to let us count the phones
breaks.do: We stop payment until the count is done. The partner agreement has this rule for exactly this case.

questions.q: Are partner phones really enrolled in the MDM?
questions.a: Yes. The phones belong to us. If a partner refuses, that tells us the partnership itself has a problem.

questions.q: Can a worker take a phone home?
questions.a: No. A phone is issued at clock-in and returned at clock-out, every day, no exceptions.

questions.q: A worker lost a phone. Do we go to the police?
questions.a: Moharam decides after he reviews the case. Any deduction follows the handbook. We go to the police only for theft, never to pressure a worker.

questions.q: Why do we use supervised mode and kiosk mode?
questions.a: The phone has one job. Supervised mode locks it to that job, and lets us find and wipe it.

lifecycle.name: Enroll
lifecycle.text: Add the phone to Apple Business Manager and Hexnode. Set it to supervised mode. Lock the collection app in kiosk mode.

lifecycle.name: Tag
lifecycle.text: Stick the asset tag on the phone. Record the serial number and the IMEI. Take photos of the condition.

lifecycle.name: Registry
lifecycle.text: One row per phone: tag, serial number, IMEI, model, storage size, condition, site, current holder, and every custody event.

lifecycle.name: Kit
lifecycle.text: The phone joins a site kit after one 30-minute test session uploads.

lifecycle.name: Issue
lifecycle.text: The phone is issued at clock-in and recorded against the device number.

lifecycle.name: Return
lifecycle.text: Back at clock-out with a condition tick: screen, port, mount, and battery.

lifecycle.name: Repair
lifecycle.text: A spare takes its place right away. Broken phones go to one repair shop once a week and come back within 48 hours.

lifecycle.name: Retire
lifecycle.text: Wiped, removed from the MDM, and its registry row closed.

kit.note: Kits are built at the store, the Central Cairo warehouse, and signed out as one whole set. Never start a site with a kit filled from another site.

count.rule: The Planning and Logistics Lead runs the count on the same day every week, at every site and hub. Look into any gap the same day. If it is still unexplained after 24 hours, put the missing phone in lost mode and report it to Moharam.

fleets.name: Delivery partners
fleets.where: Hotels in four cities, Mansoura, and their own sites
